# Description

Core script to run the benchmark and generate paper figures.

Notebook-specific helpers are sourced from `src/notebooks/benchmark_analysis.R`;
analysis settings, result loading, and figure assembly remain below.

## Inputs

-   `ECODA_BENCHMARK_RELEASE_RDS` and `ECODA_BENCHMARK_RELEASE_MD5` name and
    checksum-bind the reviewed release control: exact
    artifact ledger, expected rows and current-input policies, per-dataset
    primary reference methods, and checksum-bound execution times. Each
    result and compact dataset metadata bundle requires its review receipt.
    Legacy aggregate entries and new standalone BL/HR results are selected
    explicitly; missing or blocked rows stop publication output.
-   Optional cell-subsetting diagnostics use their explicitly selected,
    run-owned compact snapshots. Full cohort H5ADs stay on HPC/NAS.

## Outputs

-   Figures for the manuscript
-   Summarized raw data for appendix (e.g. cell type compositions)

# ---------------------------------------------------------------

# Load libraries and set parameters

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE}
# Setup: See README.md for initial environment setup
if (basename(getwd()) == "notebooks") {
  setwd("..")
  if (file.exists(".Rprofile")) source(".Rprofile")
}
source("src/utils/load_all_functions.R")
source("src/utils/analysis_release.R")
source("src/utils/evaluation_scores.R")
source("src/notebooks/benchmark_analysis.R", local = TRUE)
datasets <- read_datasets_json(view = "benchmark_analysis")
datasets <- datasets[vapply(datasets, function(x) isTRUE(x$use_for_benchmark), logical(1))]
# ============================================================
# ANALYSIS SCOPE — select which methods + datasets the analysis includes.
#   analysis_scope:    "preprint" = methods and datasets evaluated in the preprint
#                      (calculated with the new pipeline, but excluding post-preprint
#                      methods/datasets);
#                      "all" / "extended" = everything currently in the pipeline.
#   analysis_methods:  NULL = all methods found in the loaded results;
#                      or exact result keys, e.g.
#                      c("ECODA_authors_HR", "MrVI_hvg2000", "QOT_hvg2000")
#   analysis_datasets: NULL = all non-debug datasets from datasets.json;
#                      or dataset keys, e.g. c("Adams", "Pelka") (allows "_debug").
# Default analysis includes all currently loaded and future benchmark methods.
# ============================================================
analysis_scope <- "all"   # "preprint" | "all" (or "extended")
analysis_methods <- NULL
analysis_requested_methods <- analysis_methods
analysis_datasets <- NULL

# Result-key regex of methods added after the preprint analysis (excluded
# when analysis_scope == "preprint"). Convention for future methods: (a) cover
# every recode map they appear in, (b) give main methods a default_methods
# regex + screening branch, and (c) add them to extended_method_regex or the
# preprint/all distinction silently stops covering them.
extended_method_regex <- "^QOT_|^PILOT-GM-VAE_"
# Dataset keys added after the preprint analysis (excluded when "preprint").
extended_datasets <- character(0)

stopifnot(analysis_scope %in% c("preprint", "extended", "all"))
if (!is.null(analysis_datasets)) {
  datasets <- datasets[names(datasets) %in% analysis_datasets]
} else {
  # Skip the _debug dataset (Joanito 5-sample subset): the `_*`-prefix
  # convention marks debug-only entries in datasets.json.
  datasets <- datasets[!grepl("^_", names(datasets))]
}
if (analysis_scope == "preprint") {
  datasets <- datasets[!names(datasets) %in% extended_datasets]
}
stopifnot(length(datasets) > 0)

dataset_display_map <- sapply(datasets, `[[`, "display_name")
if ("Gongsharma_cmv_young_males" %in% names(dataset_display_map)) {
  dataset_display_map["GongSharma"] <- dataset_display_map[["Gongsharma_cmv_young_males"]]
}
# The internal key stays Gongsharma_cmv_young_males (HPC bundle/feather file
# names use it); figures display it as GongSharma.
# Set paths. Default: LOCAL mirror of the NAS benchmark result layout pulled
# into ./data (`data/benchmark/{results,embeddings,pseudobulks}`). This
# notebook reads no full benchmark H5ADs: metadata bundles and a verified
# compact composition snapshot are the only inputs needed for derived loads.
# Worker inputs remain on the authoritative HPC/NAS paths; this notebook
# consumes only compact metadata/composition artifacts.
path_nas_project <- file.path(getwd(), "data")
# path_nas_project <- file.path("", "Volumes", "Shared", "Projects", "ECODA_paper")
# HPC-computed R benchmark results (Pipeline A methods incl. composition,
# <ds>_metadata.rds bundles, trans/zeroimp, rsynced by the submit scripts to
# ${NAS_TARGET_DIR}/benchmark/).
path_nas_benchmark <- file.path(path_nas_project, "benchmark", "results")
# Python-method sample distance/embedding feathers (MrVI/PILOT/scPoli/
# QOT/PILOT-GM-VAE) and the merged execution_times.feather.
path_nas_embeddings <- file.path(path_nas_project, "benchmark", "embeddings")
path_data <- file.path(getwd(), "data")
path_plots <- file.path(getwd(), "plots")

# All aggregate comparisons use five equally weighted metrics after min–max
# scaling within dataset/view/evaluation/metric. LISI is already separation.
benchmark_metrics <- evaluation_metrics()
base_metrics <- benchmark_metrics
stopifnot(identical(benchmark_metrics, names(score_label_map)))

# Methods treated as "default" (highlighted in the parameter-screening
# figures): main methods at their default parameter setting. The regex is
# matched against the *recoded* method names in the screening figure.
default_methods <- c(
  "ECODA_authors_HR\\b",
  "MOFA_hvg2000_factors15",
  "Pseudobulk_hvg2000\\b",
  "Pseudobulk_CT_HR_hvg2000",
  "PILOT_hvg2000_HR\\b",
  "scITD_hvg2000_factors5",
  "scPoli_hvg2000_embdims15_HR\\b",
  "GloScope_hvg2000_pcadims30",
  "GloProp",
  "MrVI_hvg2000",
  "QOT_hvg2000_HR\\b",
  "PILOT-GM-VAE_hvg2000_HR\\b"
)
default_methods_regex <- paste(default_methods, collapse = "|")

set.seed(123)

data(example_data)
test <- calc_freq(example_data$Zhang$cell_counts$authors_HR)
```

# Create results list to fill

```{r}
# No result_list.rds persistence (Option A): every knit starts fresh and
# reloads all HPC bundles (fast readRDS) — a stale file on disk must not be
# read back in, and nothing writes it anymore (the old stale-in-memory
# clobber hazard is gone; knits are fully deterministic).
result_list <- list()
```

# ---------------------------------------------------------------

# Process datasets

NOTE: Pre-processed (e.g. including cell type annotation, clustering, etc.) dataset .rds files (with shortened names) are deposited online at: <https://doi.org/10.6084/m9.figshare.31456522> . They can be used as input for the following code (after adapting the names according to the names defined in `"datasets.json"`):

```{r message=FALSE, warning=FALSE, echo=FALSE, results='hide'}
# The control RDS contains ledger, expected_scope, reference_method_key and
# execution_times = list(artifact_path=ABS, md5=MD5). Each dataset's reviewed
# __dataset_metadata__ row supplies its existing compact composition metadata;
# optional __trans__/__zeroimp__ rows supply the maintained diagnostic tables.
# Required new BL/HR/Stephenson rows are never discovered in old directories.
benchmark_release_path <- Sys.getenv("ECODA_BENCHMARK_RELEASE_RDS", unset = "")
if (!nzchar(benchmark_release_path) || !file.exists(benchmark_release_path)) {
  stop("Set ECODA_BENCHMARK_RELEASE_RDS to an explicit reviewed release control; production figures remain blocked.")
}
benchmark_release_md5 <- Sys.getenv("ECODA_BENCHMARK_RELEASE_MD5", unset = "")
benchmark_control <- read_benchmark_analysis_control(benchmark_release_path, benchmark_release_md5)
benchmark_release <- load_benchmark_analysis_release(benchmark_control, datasets)
# Validate the declared timing artifact before any figure chunk is reached.
benchmark_release_times <- read_benchmark_execution_times(benchmark_control)
result_list <- benchmark_release$results
benchmark_expected_grid <- benchmark_release$expected_grid
HVGs <- c(1000, 2000, 3000)
factors_test <- c(2, 3, 5, 10, 15)
release_statistics <- benchmark_release$statistics
release_statistics$dataset[release_statistics$dataset == "Gongsharma_cmv_young_males"] <- "GongSharma"
n_cells_by_ds <- as.list(setNames(release_statistics$n_cells, release_statistics$dataset))
ds_stats_list <- split(release_statistics, release_statistics$dataset)
ds_stats_df <- bind_rows(ds_stats_list)
# All additional method variants must be explicit rows in the same ledger.
# No independent derived-root opt-in may append an unreviewed generation.
cell_depth_release_path <- Sys.getenv("ECODA_CELL_DEPTH_RELEASE_RDS", unset = "")
cell_depth_release_md5 <- Sys.getenv("ECODA_CELL_DEPTH_RELEASE_MD5", unset = "")
cell_subsetting_requested <- nzchar(cell_depth_release_path)
cell_subsetting_results <- NULL
if (nzchar(Sys.getenv("ECODA_DERIVED_CELL_SUBSETTING_DIR", unset = "")))
  stop("Historical cell-depth directories cannot qualify as the current five-metric release; use ECODA_CELL_DEPTH_RELEASE_RDS/MD5")
if (cell_subsetting_requested) {
  expected_labels_by_dataset <- setNames(lapply(names(datasets), function(ds)
    result_list$bmark[[ds]][[benchmark_control$reference_method_key[[ds]]]]$labels), names(datasets))
  expected_samples_by_dataset <- lapply(expected_labels_by_dataset, names)
  expected_current_inputs <- setNames(lapply(names(datasets), function(ds) {
    rows <- benchmark_control$expected_scope[benchmark_control$expected_scope$dataset == ds &
      benchmark_control$expected_scope$view == "benchmark_analysis" &
      benchmark_control$expected_scope$method_key == "ECODA_authors_HR", , drop = FALSE]
    if (nrow(rows) != 1L) stop("Cell-depth input requires the current reviewed HR identity: ", ds)
    rows$current_input_md5[[1L]]
  }), names(datasets))
  cell_subsetting_results <- load_derived_cell_subsetting(NULL, NULL, names(datasets), expected_samples_by_dataset,
    release_control_path = cell_depth_release_path, release_control_md5 = cell_depth_release_md5,
    expected_labels_by_dataset = expected_labels_by_dataset, expected_current_inputs = expected_current_inputs)
}

```

# Plot benchmark results

## Save and flatten the nested list into a DataFrame

```{r}
bmark_result_list <- result_list[["bmark"]]

bmark_result_list$GongSharma <- bmark_result_list$Gongsharma_cmv_young_males
bmark_result_list$Gongsharma_cmv_young_males <- NULL

df_benchmark <- benchmark_release$scores
df_benchmark$dataset[df_benchmark$dataset == "Gongsharma_cmv_young_males"] <- "GongSharma"
benchmark_expected_grid$dataset[benchmark_expected_grid$dataset == "Gongsharma_cmv_young_males"] <- "GongSharma"

# Drop old modularity score method
df_benchmark <- df_benchmark[!df_benchmark$score == "mod_score", ]

# Resolve the analysis scope: analysis_methods NULL = all methods found in
# the loaded results; "preprint" drops the extended (post-preprint) methods.
# Runs BEFORE the factor() below so the method levels are exactly the scoped
# set.
if (is.null(analysis_methods)) {
  analysis_methods <- unique(as.character(df_benchmark$method))
}
if (analysis_scope == "preprint") {
  analysis_methods <- analysis_methods[
    !grepl(extended_method_regex, analysis_methods)
  ]
}
df_benchmark <- df_benchmark[df_benchmark$method %in% analysis_methods, ]
benchmark_main_normalization_methods <- methods_in_scope(benchmark_main_method_keys)
benchmark_extended_normalization_methods <- methods_in_scope(benchmark_extended_method_keys)
# Supplementary MDS panels use Figure 2A's main-method pool, including NULL.
# Figure 2B uses the documented extended pool because it also displays frequency.

hitme_flagged_ds <- names(datasets)[vapply(names(datasets), function(k) "hitme" %in% flag_status_for(k), logical(1))]
scatomic_flagged_ds <- names(datasets)[vapply(names(datasets), function(k) "scatomic" %in% flag_status_for(k), logical(1))]
if (length(hitme_flagged_ds) > 0 || length(scatomic_flagged_ds) > 0) {
  message("not_suitable_for_auto_annotation: HiTME excluded for [",
          paste(hitme_flagged_ds, collapse = ", "), "], scATOMIC excluded for [",
          paste(scatomic_flagged_ds, collapse = ", "),
          "] in the annotation-comparison figures")
}
```

## Plot results

### All methods (overview)

```{r fig.height=8, fig.width=16}
df_benchmark %>%
  filter(score %in% benchmark_metrics) %>%
  group_by(score, method) %>%
  summarize(mean = mean(value), sem = sd(value) / sqrt(length(value))) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  ggplot(aes(x = method, y = mean)) + 
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge()) +
  geom_errorbar(aes(ymin=mean-sem, ymax=mean+sem), width=0.2, colour="black", alpha=0.9) +
  labs(x = "", y = "") +
  theme_minimal() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 75, vjust = 1, hjust=1)) +
  facet_grid(scales = "free",
             rows = vars(score),
             labeller = labeller(score = as_labeller(score_facet_labels)))
ggsave(file.path(path_plots, "benchmark_summary_barplot_separatescores_bars.pdf"),
       width = 14,
       height = 7)
```

```{r fig.height=4, fig.width=4}
  expected_grid = benchmark_expected_grid) %>%
  # -- Recoding names --
  mutate(method = recode(method,
                         "ECODA_authors_HR" = "ECODA_authors",
                         "ECODA_authors_HR_NULL" = "Shuffled_baseline",
                         "ECODA_HiTME_HR_layer2" = "ECODA_automated",

# 4. Generate the Plot
# We filter for ANOSIM and use 'scaled_value' instead of 'value'
df_plot_scaled %>%
  filter(score == "anosim_score") %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(method, scaled_value, .desc = TRUE, .fun = mean), 
             y = scaled_value)) + # Use the scaled column
  
  # Error bars and Mean Bar
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar", fill = "white", color = "black") +
  
  # Individual Points and connecting lines (Paired data)
  geom_point(position = "identity", alpha = 0.6, size = 0.8) +
  geom_line(aes(group = dataset), color = "grey20", alpha = 0.2) +
  
  # Statistical Test
  stat_compare_means(
    ref.group = "ECODA_authors",
    method = "wilcox.test",
    paired = TRUE,
    angle = 25,
    vjust = 1,
    aes(label = sprintf("%5.2f", as.numeric(..p.format..)))
  ) +
  
  # Adjust Y-axis (Since data is 0-1, we set limit slightly higher for p-values)
  ylim(c(0, 1.15)) + 
  
  labs(x = "", y = "Separation score\n(Scaled ANOSIM score)") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 65, vjust = 1, hjust = 1))
ggsave(file.path(path_plots, "benchmark_summary_barplot_ANOSIM_minmaxscaled_mainmethods_refECODA.pdf"),
       width = 4.5,
       height = 4.5)
```

```{r fig.height=6, fig.width=5}
  ungroup() %>%
  
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(method, mean_value, .desc = TRUE),
             y = value, 
             fill = ifelse(grepl(default_methods_regex, method), "cornflowerblue", "gray70"))) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar") +
  labs(x = "", y = "") +
  theme_classic2(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_markdown(angle = 65, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
  panel.grid.major.y = element_line(size = 0.25, linetype = 'solid',
                                colour = "lightgrey"), 
  panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(size = 0.25, linetype = 'solid',
                                colour = "lightgrey")) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  # ylim(c(-0.4, 1)) +
  facet_grid(scales = "free_x",
             space='free',
             rows = vars(score),
             labeller = as_labeller(score_facet_labels))
ggsave(file.path(path_plots, "benchmark_summary_barplot_allmetricscombined_mainmethods_with_bad_baselines.pdf"),
       width = 4.5,
       height = 6.5)
```

### Bassez: descriptive feature and PCA diagnostics

The reviewed HPC renderer uses saved current author-HR and pseudobulk result
features, with centered, unscaled PCA and label-blind loading selection. E/NE
means **Expander/Non-expander T-cell clonal expansion**, not clinical response.
Current HR coverage and cell totals are verified against the approved dataset
metadata and recovered counts; no historical 33-category/24,139-cell baseline
is substituted. The exported gene tables contain bounded aggregate statistics
and PCA loadings, never sample-by-gene expression or pseudobulk matrices.
Sensitivity statistics remain exploratory and use no permutation tests.

```{r bassez-feature-diagnostics, fig.height=6, fig.width=12, results='asis'}
    names(datasets), benchmark_control$expected_scope)
}

  df_results_list[[paste0("Bassez_", table_name)]] <- pca_render$tables[[table_name]]
}
```

### Bassez: opt-in matched all-cell composition comparison

The original authors-HR composition covers 24,139 cells in 33 retained fine
categories, whereas all-cell pseudobulk covers 74,948 cells in the same 26
samples. Merely appending nonimmune broad categories to HR misses T/myeloid
cells without a retained subtype. This comparison instead uses the original
metadata cross-tab: retain valid author `cellSubType`, otherwise use author
`cellType`. Missing subtypes are actual missing values or the exact strings
`NA`, `nan`, `None`, `Unknown`, and the empty string. It verifies the original
HR and broad LR counts **exactly for every sample/category** before including
all cells. The source broad/fine annotations are not a strict hierarchy:
for example, fine `pDC` occurs under both `Myeloid_cell` and `pDC`, and fine
`ASDC`/`cDC2` can occur under broad `pDC`. Fine labels are preserved regardless
of broad parentage; no such cells are discarded or reassigned. The original
fine `pDC` label and broad fallback `pDC` denote the same population, so the
literal fine-otherwise-broad rule combines 241 fine-labelled and 10 fallback
cells into one `pDC` category (251 cells). This verified overlap produces 40
mixed categories: 33 fine + 8 fallback − 1 shared `pDC`. Fallback coverage
still counts those 10 cells as fallback; other unsupported label collisions
stop the comparison rather than silently pooling distinct categories.

This historical comparison is manual HPC-only (`eval=FALSE`) and requires a
separately approved original HR33 source. It is outside current mixed-HR
publication intake. `ECODA_BASSEZ_ANNOTATION_COUNTS` names a compact
CSV with columns `Sample,cellType,cellSubType,count`. Its adjacent file
`<CSV path>.md5` must contain one bare 32-character MD5 digest, with optional
surrounding whitespace. This compact input is a tabulation of original
metadata, not expression data. No remote input is required by the rest of
the notebook. Each opted-in run writes a new
`plots/Bassez_matched_cells_<timestamp>` directory and refuses overwrites.
The checksum and input path are recorded beside its output tables.

All categories enter count+0.5 row-wise CLR, Euclidean distance and centered,
unscaled PCA without biological labels. The comparison reports ANOSIM R
without permutations, k=3 modularity, and mean Ward/PAM ARI from full-feature
distances, not the first two PCs. E/NE denotes **Expander/Non-expander T-cell
expansion, not clinical response**. These are descriptive separation scores:
matching cells removes the HR/all-cell scope difference, but does not imply
a causal or clinical interpretation. This does not replace pseudobulk on the
exact original HR33 cell subset; that requires expression-level subsetting.

```{r bassez-matched-allcell-comparison, eval=FALSE, fig.height=6, fig.width=18, results='asis'}
bassez_annotation_path <- Sys.getenv("ECODA_BASSEZ_ANNOTATION_COUNTS", unset = "")
if (!nzchar(bassez_annotation_path)) {
  message("Skipping matched all-cell comparison: ECODA_BASSEZ_ANNOTATION_COUNTS is unset.")
} else {
  bassez_matched_cells <- local({
    input_path <- normalizePath(bassez_annotation_path, mustWork = TRUE)
    checksum_path <- paste0(input_path, ".md5")
    if (!file.exists(checksum_path)) {
      stop("Missing adjacent bare MD5 checksum file: ", checksum_path)
    }
    expected_md5 <- trimws(paste(readLines(checksum_path, warn = FALSE),
                                collapse = "\n"))
    actual_md5 <- unname(tools::md5sum(input_path))
    if (!grepl("^[0-9a-fA-F]{32}$", expected_md5) ||
        is.na(actual_md5) || tolower(expected_md5) != tolower(actual_md5)) {
      stop("Bassez annotation cross-tab MD5 does not match its checksum file.")
    }
    if (!exists("result_list") ||
        is.null(result_list[["bmark"]][["Bassez"]])) {
      stop("Opted-in all-cell comparison requires loaded Bassez method bundles.")
    }
    annotation_counts <- utils::read.csv(
      input_path, stringsAsFactors = FALSE, check.names = FALSE,
      na.strings = NULL,
      colClasses = c(Sample = "character", cellType = "character",
                     cellSubType = "character", count = "numeric")
    )
    bundles <- result_list[["bmark"]][["Bassez"]]
    comparison <- bassez_allcell_comparison(annotation_counts, bundles)
    method_titles <- c(
      ECODA_authors_HR = "ECODA authors HR (24,139 cells)",
      ECODA_authors_mixed_allcells = "ECODA mixed all cells (74,948 cells)",
      Pseudobulk_hvg2000 = "Pseudobulk HVG2000 (74,948 cells)"
    )
    label_names <- c(E = "Expander (E)", NE = "Non-expander (NE)")
    plot_labels <- factor(unname(label_names[comparison$labels]),
                          levels = unname(label_names))
    panels <- lapply(names(method_titles), function(method) {
      x <- if (method == "ECODA_authors_mixed_allcells") {
        comparison$feat_mat
      } else {
        bundles[[method]]$feat_mat
      }
      plot_pca(
        feat_mat = x, labels = plot_labels, scale. = FALSE,
        n_ct_show = 7, invisible = "quali", repel = TRUE,
        coord_equal = FALSE, title = method_titles[[method]],
        cluster_score = FALSE, mod_score = FALSE,
        sil_score = FALSE, anosim_score = FALSE
      )
    })
    pca_plot <- patchwork::wrap_plots(panels, nrow = 1) +
      patchwork::plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
      patchwork::plot_annotation(
        title = "Bassez: HR versus matched all-cell composition and pseudobulk",
        subtitle = "E/NE is expansion, not clinical response; seven label-blind contribution arrows per panel"
      )
    print(knitr::kable(comparison$methods, digits = 4,
                       caption = "Full-feature separation; no ANOSIM permutation tests."))
    print(knitr::kable(comparison$coverage, digits = 4,
                       caption = "Original metadata coverage: fine subtype versus broad fallback."))
    print(pca_plot)
    output_dir <- file.path(
      if (exists("path_plots")) path_plots else file.path(getwd(), "plots"),
      paste0("Bassez_matched_cells_", format(Sys.time(), "%Y%m%dT%H%M%S"))
    )
    if (file.exists(output_dir)) {
      stop("Refusing to overwrite matched-cell outputs: ", output_dir)
    }
    if (!dir.create(output_dir, recursive = TRUE)) {
      stop("Could not create matched-cell output directory: ", output_dir)
    }
    for (table_name in c("methods", "coverage", "fallback_counts")) {
      utils::write.csv(comparison[[table_name]],
                       file.path(output_dir, paste0("Bassez_", table_name, ".csv")),
                       row.names = FALSE)
    }
    for (table_name in c("raw_counts", "counts")) {
      count_table <- data.frame(
        Sample = rownames(comparison[[table_name]]),
        comparison[[table_name]], check.names = FALSE, row.names = NULL
      )
      utils::write.csv(count_table,
                       file.path(output_dir, paste0("Bassez_", table_name, ".csv")),
                       row.names = FALSE)
    }
    utils::write.csv(
      data.frame(input_path = input_path, md5 = actual_md5),
      file.path(output_dir, "Bassez_annotation_source.csv"), row.names = FALSE
    )
    for (extension in c("pdf", "png")) {
      ggplot2::ggsave(
        file.path(output_dir, paste0("Bassez_matched_cells_PCA.", extension)),
        plot = pca_plot, width = 18, height = 6, dpi = 300
      )
    }
    attr(comparison, "output_dir") <- output_dir
    comparison
  })
}
```

#### Presentation: Adams annotation correspondence matrix

This cell-level correspondence table compares Authors_HR (columns) with the
persisted, non-Harmony Leiden_res_0.4 clusters (rows); cluster IDs are not
predicted author labels. Each author column sums to 100% before rounding.
Clusters are hierarchically ordered by their author-type composition; author
types are grouped by their strongest matching cluster, then decreasing match.
All entries, including zeros, show two decimal places. The large-format PDF
retains all 38 author types and 21 clusters rather than merging annotations.
The ordering exposes a stair-step diagonal band without merging categories or
changing percentages; several author types can share the same Leiden cluster.

The notebook reads only compact counts. Generate them once with the repository
Pixi Python and `src/extract_adams_annotation_correspondence.py --h5ad
<NAS-Adams-benchmark-H5AD> --output-dir
data/derived/adams_annotation_correspondence_res0.4_20261023`. The exporter reads
only the configured author annotation, the persisted Leiden column, and cell IDs, never expression or
embedding values. Its manifest records source identity and selected-metadata
SHA256; it does not claim a fresh whole-H5AD checksum.

```{r adams_annotation_correspondence, fig.width=18, fig.height=12}
adams_correspondence_override <- Sys.getenv(
  "ECODA_ADAMS_CORRESPONDENCE_DIR", unset = NA_character_
)
adams_correspondence_root <- if (is.na(adams_correspondence_override)) {
  file.path(path_data, "derived", "adams_annotation_correspondence_res0.4_20261023")
} else {
  adams_correspondence_override
}
if (is.na(adams_correspondence_override) && !dir.exists(adams_correspondence_root)) {
  message("Optional Adams correspondence figure skipped: no compact export at ",
          adams_correspondence_root)
} else {
  adams_correspondence_manifest <- jsonlite::read_json(
    file.path(adams_correspondence_root, "manifest.json"), simplifyVector = TRUE
  )
  adams_correspondence_path <- file.path(adams_correspondence_root, "counts.csv")
  adams_correspondence_identity <- .derived_sidecar(adams_correspondence_path)
  stopifnot(
    identical(adams_correspondence_manifest$dataset, "Adams"),
    identical(adams_correspondence_manifest$view, "benchmark_analysis"),
    identical(adams_correspondence_manifest$author_column,
              datasets[["Adams"]]$cell_type_high_res),
    identical(adams_correspondence_manifest$leiden_column,
              "leiden_res_0.4_benchmark_analysis_hvg2000"),
    identical(adams_correspondence_identity$md5,
              adams_correspondence_manifest$counts_md5),
    adams_correspondence_identity$size == adams_correspondence_manifest$counts_size
  )
  adams_correspondence_counts <- as.matrix(read.csv(
    adams_correspondence_path, row.names = 1, check.names = FALSE
  ))
  stopifnot(
    is.numeric(adams_correspondence_counts),
    all(is.finite(adams_correspondence_counts)),
    all(adams_correspondence_counts >= 0),
    all(adams_correspondence_counts == floor(adams_correspondence_counts)),
    nrow(adams_correspondence_counts) == adams_correspondence_manifest$n_author_types,
    ncol(adams_correspondence_counts) == adams_correspondence_manifest$n_leiden_clusters,
    sum(adams_correspondence_counts) == adams_correspondence_manifest$n_cells,
    all(rowSums(adams_correspondence_counts) > 0),
    all(colSums(adams_correspondence_counts) > 0)
  )
  # Similar cluster compositions stay adjacent; names do not determine order.
  adams_cluster_purity <- sweep(
    adams_correspondence_counts, 2, colSums(adams_correspondence_counts), "/"
  )
  adams_cluster_order <- hclust(
    dist(t(adams_cluster_purity)), method = "average"
  )$order
  adams_correspondence_counts <- adams_correspondence_counts[
    , adams_cluster_order, drop = FALSE
  ]
  adams_author_percent <- 100 * prop.table(adams_correspondence_counts, 1)
  adams_author_order <- order(
    max.col(adams_author_percent, ties.method = "first"),
    -apply(adams_author_percent, 1, max)
  )
  adams_correspondence_counts <- adams_correspondence_counts[
    adams_author_order, , drop = FALSE
  ]
  adams_correspondence_percent <- 100 * prop.table(adams_correspondence_counts, 1)
  stopifnot(all(abs(rowSums(adams_correspondence_percent) - 100) < 1e-8))
  adams_correspondence_df <- as.data.frame(
    as.table(adams_correspondence_percent),
    responseName = "percentage", stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
  names(adams_correspondence_df)[1:2] <- c("Authors_HR", "Leiden_res_0.4")
  adams_correspondence_df$Authors_HR <- factor(
    adams_correspondence_df$Authors_HR,
    levels = rownames(adams_correspondence_counts)
  )
  adams_correspondence_df$Leiden_res_0.4 <- factor(
    adams_correspondence_df$Leiden_res_0.4,
    levels = rev(colnames(adams_correspondence_counts))
  )
  p_adams_correspondence <- ggplot(
    adams_correspondence_df,
    aes(x = Authors_HR, y = Leiden_res_0.4, fill = percentage)
  ) +
    geom_tile(color = "white", linewidth = 0.15) +
    geom_text(
      aes(label = sprintf("%.2f", percentage),
          color = ifelse(percentage >= 50, "white",
                         ifelse(percentage == 0, "grey65", "black"))),
      size = 2.8
    ) +
    scale_color_identity() +
    scale_fill_gradient(
      low = "white", high = "#2166AC", limits = c(0, 100),
      breaks = c(0, 25, 50, 75, 100), name = "% of author type"
    ) +
    scale_x_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    scale_y_discrete(expand = c(0, 0)) +
    coord_fixed() +
    labs(
      title = "Adams: Authors_HR and Leiden_res_0.4 annotation correspondence",
      subtitle = paste0(
        format(sum(adams_correspondence_counts), big.mark = ","),
        " cells | Column-normalized percentages; each author type sums to 100%"
      ),
      x = "Authors_HR cell type (grouped by strongest Leiden match)",
      y = "Leiden_res_0.4 cluster"
    ) +
    theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
    theme(
      panel.grid = element_blank(),
      axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1, size = 10),
      axis.text.y = element_text(size = 10),
      plot.margin = margin(12, 18, 12, 18)
    )
  print(p_adams_correspondence)
  ggsave(
    file.path(path_plots, "presentation_Figure_3_B_correspondance_matrix.pdf"),
    plot = p_adams_correspondence, width = 18, height = 12
  )
}
```

```{r fig.height=8, fig.width=14}
filter_methods <- c(

  "ECODA_seuratres_20"
)

# default_methods / default_methods_regex are defined once in the setup chunk
# (highlighting of default methods in this screening figure).

supp_fig_2_scores <- base_metrics
supp_fig_2_score_labels <- c(
  "anosim_score" = "ANOSIM",
  "mod_knn3_score" = "Modularity",
  "cluster_score" = "ARI",
  "sil_score" = "Silhouette",
  "lisi_score" = "LISI"
)

supp_fig_2_plot <- df_benchmark %>%
  filter(score %in% supp_fig_2_scores) %>%
  filter(!grepl("HiTME|scATOMIC|seuratres|ECODA_authors_HR_NULL|ECODA_authors_LR|ECODA_deconv|Freq_highres|varexp|varcts|Avg_PCA|combo|schvg", method)
  ) %>%
  filter(
    if_else(grepl("scPoli", method), grepl("highres|lowres", method), TRUE)
  ) %>%
  # filter(method %in% filter_methods) %>%
  # mutate(method = recode(method,
  #                        "MOFA_2_factors" = "MOFA",
  #                        "scITD_2_factors" = "scITD",
  #                        "ECODA_highres" = "ECODA")) %>%
  
  # CREATE THE FACETING GROUP COLUMN
  mutate(
    score = factor(score, levels = supp_fig_2_scores),
    method_plot = case_when(
      grepl("^ECODA_", method) ~ "ECODA",
      grepl("^(MOFA_|MOFAcellulaR_)", method) ~ "MOFA",
      grepl("^MrVI_", method) ~ "MrVI",
      grepl("^scITD_", method) ~ "scITD",
      grepl("^GloScope_", method) ~ "GloScope",
      grepl("^GloProp", method) ~ "GloScope",
      grepl("^PILOT_", method) ~ "PILOT",
      grepl("^PILOT-GM-VAE_", method) ~ "PILOT-GM-VAE",
      grepl("^QOT_", method) ~ "QOT",
      grepl("^scPoli_", method) ~ "scPoli",
      grepl("^Pseudobulk_", method) ~ "Pseudobulk",
      TRUE ~ method # Keep any other simple names as they are
    ),
    
    method_plot = factor(method_plot, 
                         levels = c("ECODA", "Pseudobulk", "MrVI", "GloScope", "GloProp",
                                    "scPoli", "MOFA", "PILOT", "scITD", "QOT",
                                    "PILOT-GM-VAE"))
  ) %>%
  
  mutate(method = method %>%
           # Swap highres/lowres
           stringr::str_replace_all(c("highres"  = "HR", 
                                      "lowres"   = "LR",
                                      "0_dims"    = "0_embdims")) %>%
           stringr::str_replace("Pseudobulk_(\\d+)_PCA_dims", "Pseudobulk_hvg2000_pcadims\\1") %>%
           stringr::str_replace("(\\d+)_PCA_dims", "pcadims\\1") %>%
           stringr::str_replace("PILOT_hvg(\\d+)", "PILOT_hvg\\1_HR") %>%
           stringr::str_replace("QOT_hvg(\\d+)", "QOT_hvg\\1_HR") %>%
           stringr::str_replace("PILOT-GM-VAE_hvg(\\d+)", "PILOT-GM-VAE_hvg\\1_HR")
  ) %>%
  
  group_by(method) %>%
  mutate(mean_value = mean(value[score == "anosim_score"])) %>%
  ungroup() %>%
  
  ggplot(aes(x = fct_reorder(method, mean_value, .desc = TRUE),
             y = value, 
             fill = ifelse(grepl(default_methods_regex, method), "cornflowerblue", "gray70"))) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar") +
  labs(x = "", y = "") +
  theme_classic2(base_size = 12) +
  theme(axis.text.x = element_markdown(angle = 90, vjust = 1, hjust = 1),
  panel.grid.major.y = element_line(size = 0.25, linetype = 'solid',
                                colour = "lightgrey"), 
  panel.grid.minor.y = element_line(size = 0.25, linetype = 'solid',
                                colour = "lightgrey")) +
  scale_fill_identity() +
  # Highlight default methods
  scale_x_discrete(labels = function(x) highlight(
    x,
    default_methods_regex,
    "black")
  ) +
  # ylim(c(-0.4, 1)) +
  facet_grid(scales = "free",
             space='free',
             rows = vars(score),
             cols = vars(method_plot), # Use the new grouping column for column faceting
             labeller = labeller(
               score = as_labeller(supp_fig_2_score_labels),
               method_plot = function(labels) sub("^PILOT-GM-VAE$", "PILOT-G-V", labels)
             ))


ggsave(file.path(path_plots, "Supp_fig_2_methodparameter_screening.pdf"),
       plot = supp_fig_2_plot,
       width = 14,
       height = 8)
```

## Figure 4 AB: Plot feature selection

Surprisingly, even at the lowest number highly variable cell types (i.e. variance explained of 10% -\> \>=2 cell types) the average biological separation is quite very high. Different daatasets can do with a different number of highly variable cell types (separation plateaus out at different levels of variance explained % and number of cell types retained).

```{r}
df_benchmark_sub <- df_benchmark %>%
  # filter(score == "anosim_score") %>%
  filter(score %in% benchmark_metrics) %>%
  filter(grepl("ECODA_authors_HR", method) & !grepl("HiTME|scATOMIC|PCA|NULL|most|least", method)) %>%
  filter(!grepl("cmv|sex", dataset)) %>%
  filter(!method == "ECODA_authors_HR_top_varexp0") %>%
  mutate(method = recode(method,
                         "ECODA_authors_HR" = "100",
                         "ECODA_authors_HR_top_varexp0" = "2most_varcts")) %>%
  mutate(method = gsub("ECODA_authors_HR", "", method)) %>%
  mutate(method = if_else(
    grepl("^_top_varexp0\\.\\d", method),
    paste0(as.integer(gsub("_top_varexp0\\.", "", method)) * 10),
    method
  )) %>%
  # mutate(method = gsub("top_varexp0", "2most_varcts", method)) %>%
  mutate(method = fct_relevel(method)) %>%
  mutate(method = factor(method, levels = rev(mixedsort(levels(method))))) %>%
  mutate(dataset = recode(dataset,
                          "GongSharma_all_age" = "GongSharma"))

df_benchmark_anosim <- df_benchmark_sub %>% filter(score == "anosim_score")

df_hvc40 <- df_benchmark_anosim[df_benchmark_anosim$method == 40 ,]
perc_tot <- c()
for (ds in df_hvc40$dataset) {
  tot <- df_benchmark_anosim$n_features[df_benchmark_anosim$dataset == ds & df_benchmark_anosim$method == 100]
  perc_tot <- c(perc_tot, round(df_hvc40$n_features[df_hvc40$dataset == ds] / tot * 100))
}

cts <- df_hvc40$n_features
print(paste0("The top ", min(cts), "-", max(cts), " cell types ", 
             "(~", min(perc_tot), "-", max(perc_tot), "% of the total) ",
             "explain 40% of the datasets' variances."))

unique(df_benchmark_sub$method)

pointsize <- 1.5

p1 <- df_benchmark_anosim %>%
  ggplot(aes(x = method, y = n_features)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = "mean_se", geom = "errorbar", width = 0.2) +
  stat_summary(fun = mean, geom = "bar", fill = "white", color = "black") +
  geom_point(aes(shape = dataset, color = dataset), size = pointsize) + # Color added for legend consistency
  scale_shape_manual(values=1:length(unique((df_benchmark_sub$dataset)))) +
  geom_line(aes(group=dataset, linetype=dataset, color = dataset), alpha = 1) +
```

```{r fig.height=15, fig.width=15}
# devtools::install_github("carmonalab/scECODA", force = TRUE)
plot_list <- list()

dss <- names(result_list[["bmark"]])

for (ds in dss) {
  counts <- result_list[["bmark"]][[ds]]$ECODA_authors_HR$counts
  meta <- data.frame(
    sample_id = names(result_list[["bmark"]][[ds]]$ECODA_authors_HR$labels),
    group = result_list[["bmark"]][[ds]]$ECODA_authors_HR$labels,
    row.names = names(result_list[["bmark"]][[ds]]$ECODA_authors_HR$labels)
  )
  ecoda_object <- ecoda(t(counts), metadata = meta, variance_explained = 0.4)
  
  if (ds == "GongSharma_all_age") {
    pt <- "GongSharma"
  } else pt <- ds
  
  p <- plot_varmean(ecoda_object, plot_title = pt)
  # print(p)
  plot_list[[ds]] <- p

  # print(p)
}
```

# Plot execution times

## Unified execution times (HPC feather + bundle rows)

```{r}
# Single source of execution times, regenerated fresh on EVERY knit (no
# data/exec_times.rds cache: a stale cache would pin old rows, e.g. NA
# mem_GB for R methods computed before the workers logged peak RAM).
#
# Established execution logs remain four columns:
# dataset/method/time_secs/mem_GB.  Schema-2 preparation workers emit global
# `prepare_pseudobulk_shared` and `prepare_pseudobulk_ct_shared_<token>` rows
# per timing context plus variant-local rows.  Shared rows are retained as
# accounting rows; they are never joined onto each pseudobulk variant.  If a
# timing-extended artifact is encountered, helpers.R validates it and uses
# variant_time_secs locally.
#
# 1. The NAS merged feather (${NAS_TARGET_DIR}/benchmark/embeddings/
#    execution_times.feather): HPC rows (R heavy methods, composition
#    methods, python methods, trans/zeroimp, prepare_pseudobulk_*).
# 2. Bundle-derived rows for methods the feather does not cover — union by
#    (dataset, method); mem_GB taken from the bundle when present.
feather_exec_times <- benchmark_release_times

bundle_exec_times <- imap_dfr(result_list[["bmark"]], ~ {
  dataset_name <- .y
  imap_dfr(.x, function(bundle, method_name) {
    execution_time_rows_from_bundle(dataset_name, method_name, bundle)
  })
})
if (ncol(bundle_exec_times) == 0L) {
  bundle_exec_times <- data.frame(
    dataset = character(),
    method = character(),
    time_secs = numeric(),
    mem_GB = numeric(),
    stringsAsFactors = FALSE
  )
}

feather_exec_times <- normalize_exec_keys(feather_exec_times)
bundle_exec_times <- normalize_exec_keys(bundle_exec_times)

feather_exec_times[[".execution_union_key"]] <-
  execution_union_key(feather_exec_times)
bundle_exec_times[[".execution_union_key"]] <-
  execution_union_key(bundle_exec_times)

# Feather rows win for ordinary dataset/method records; bundle rows fill
# methods absent from the feather while retaining distinct shared identities.
bundle_only <- bundle_exec_times %>%
  anti_join(
    feather_exec_times %>% dplyr::select(.execution_union_key),
    by = ".execution_union_key"
  )
exec_times <- bind_rows(
  feather_exec_times %>% dplyr::select(-.execution_union_key),
  bundle_only %>% dplyr::select(-.execution_union_key)
) %>%
  deduplicate_exec_times()

# n_cells per dataset (from the metadata bundles via the dataset loop;
# display keys).
n_cells_lookup <- unlist(n_cells_by_ds)
exec_times$n_cells <- n_cells_lookup[exec_times$dataset]

# NAS feather covers all benchmark datasets; keep only this run's datasets
# (n_cells_by_ds keys are display keys, matching exec_times$dataset).
exec_times <- exec_times[exec_times$dataset %in% names(n_cells_by_ds), ]

# A report-level total has one shared preparation charge per timing identity.
# Keep this explicit object available to downstream summaries; method-level
# plots below continue to use variant-local time_secs.
exec_time_summary <- summarize_exec_times(exec_times)

```

## Execution-time totals (shared preparation counted once)

```{r}
# Keep the global shared preparation charge separate from method-level rows.
# This table is the report's authoritative total and never joins shared work
# to every method.
exec_time_summary_display <- exec_time_summary %>%
  transmute(
    Dataset = dataset,
    `Variant/local (s)` = variant_time_secs,
    `Shared preparation (s)` = shared_time_secs,
    `Legacy inclusive (s)` = legacy_inclusive_time_secs,
    `Total (s)` = total_time_secs
  )
knitr::kable(
  exec_time_summary_display,
  digits = 2,
  caption = "Execution-time totals by dataset; shared preparation is counted once per timing identity."
)
```

## Supp fig 14: Plot

```{r}
filter_methods <- methods_in_scope(c(
  "ECODA_authors_HR",

  # "Pseudobulk_hvg2000",
  "Pseudobulk_hvg2000",
  
  "MOFA_hvg2000_factors15",

  "GloScope_hvg2000_pcadims30",
  "GloProp",
  "MrVI_hvg2000",
  "scPoli_hvg2000_dims15_highres",
  "PILOT_hvg2000",
  "QOT_hvg2000",
  "PILOT-GM-VAE_hvg2000"
))


# --- 1. Clean Data ---
plot_data <- exec_times %>%
  # prepare_pseudobulk_shared is retained in exec_times for global accounting,
  # never as a plotted method variant.
  filter(
    method %in% filter_methods,
    !.execution_is_shared_timing_method(method)
  ) %>%
  # filter(!dataset %in% c("GongSharma_all_cmv", "GongSharma_all_sex")) %>%
  mutate(method = recode(method,
                         "ECODA_authors_HR" = "ECODA",
                         "Pseudobulk_hvg2000" = "Pseudobulk",
                         "MOFA_hvg2000_factors15" = "MOFA",
                         "scITD_hvg2000_factors5" = "scITD",
                         "GloScope_hvg2000_pcadims30" = "GloScope",
                         "MrVI_hvg2000" = "MrVI",
                         "scPoli_hvg2000_dims15_highres" = "scPoli",
                         "PILOT_hvg2000" = "PILOT",
                         "QOT_hvg2000" = "QOT",
                         "PILOT-GM-VAE_hvg2000" = "PILOT-GM-VAE"))

regression_lines <- fit_log_log_lines(plot_data, "time_secs")
line_ends <- regression_lines %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(
    max_x = max(n_cells),
    pred_y = fitted[which.max(n_cells)],
    .groups = "drop"
  )
line_ends_log <- spread_log_label_y(
  line_ends %>%
    mutate(
      log_max_x = log10(max_x),
      log_pred_y = log10(pred_y)
    ),
  min_gap = 0.22
)
line_ends_raw <- line_ends_log %>%
  mutate(
    endpoint_x = 10^log_max_x,
    endpoint_y = 10^log_pred_y,
    label_x = 10^log_label_x,
    label_y = 10^log_label_y
  )
plot_x_breaks <- c(1e5, 3e5, 1e6)
plot_y_breaks <- c(1, 10, 100, 1000, 10000)

ggplot(
  plot_data,
  aes(x = n_cells, y = time_secs, color = method)
) +
  annotation_logticks(sides = "bl", color = "grey80") +
  geom_point(shape = 4, size = 1, stroke = 1.25, alpha = 0.5) +
  geom_line(
    data = regression_lines,
    aes(x = n_cells, y = fitted, color = method),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    linewidth = 0.7
  ) +
  geom_segment(
    data = line_ends_raw,
    aes(
      x = endpoint_x,
      y = endpoint_y,
      xend = label_x,
      yend = label_y
    ),
    inherit.aes = FALSE,
    color = "grey50",
    linewidth = 0.2
  ) +
  geom_text(
    data = line_ends_raw,
    aes(
      x = label_x,
      y = label_y,
      label = method,
      color = method
    ),
    hjust = 0,
    size = 4,
    show.legend = FALSE
  ) +
  labs(x = "Number of cells", y = "Time (s)") +
  theme_minimal() +
  scale_x_log10(
    breaks = plot_x_breaks,
    labels = function(x) sapply(x, scientific_A_10n),
    limits = c(
      min(plot_data$n_cells),
      max(plot_data$n_cells) * 10^0.65
    )
  ) +
  scale_y_log10(
    breaks = plot_y_breaks,
    labels = trans_format("log10", math_format(10^.x))
  ) +
  theme(legend.position = "none")

ggsave(file.path(path_plots, "Supp_fig_14_benchmark_exec_times.pdf"),
       width = 6.0,
       height = 3.5, limitsize = FALSE)
```

```{r fig.height=8, fig.width=14}
  output_file = "Presentation_benchmark_extended.pdf",
  output_dir = path_plots,
  plot_width = 14,
  plot_height = 8,
  method_width = 8,
  overall_col_name = "Metrics Mean",
  include_rank = TRUE,
  overall_legend_title = "Overall",
  overall_legend_labels = c(".         Worst", rep("", 9), "Best       .")
)
```

```{r message=FALSE}
# --- 0. CLEAN DATA (self-contained: same filter/recode as Figure 2A, built
# locally so this chunk has no cross-chunk dependency on clean_data). All
# score columns are kept (no score_set restriction) — the correlation matrix
# below includes Silhouette and LISI.
filter_methods <- methods_in_scope(c(
  "ECODA_authors_HR",
  "ECODA_authors_HR_NULL",

  "QOT_hvg2000",
  "PILOT-GM-VAE_hvg2000"
))

benchmark_method_recode <- c(
  "ECODA_authors_HR" = "ECODA",
  "ECODA_authors_HR_NULL" = "Shuffled_baseline",
  "Pseudobulk_hvg2000" = "Pseudobulk",
  "MOFA_hvg2000_factors15" = "MOFA",
  "scITD_hvg2000_factors5" = "scITD",
  "MrVI_hvg2000" = "MrVI",
  "scPoli_hvg2000_dims15_highres" = "scPoli",
  "PILOT_hvg2000" = "PILOT",
  "GloScope_hvg2000_pcadims30" = "GloScope",
  "QOT_hvg2000" = "QOT",
  "PILOT-GM-VAE_hvg2000" = "PILOT-GM-VAE"
)
clean_data <- prepare_benchmark_data(
  df_results = df_benchmark,
  exec_times = exec_times,

)

# --- 1. PREPARE WIDE DATA ---
metrics <- unname(score_label_map[base_metrics])
mean_score_components <- metrics

df_wide <- clean_data %>%
  pivot_wider(
    id_cols = c(dataset, method),
    names_from = score,
    values_from = value
  )
mean_score_data <- dplyr::select(df_wide, all_of(mean_score_components))
stopifnot(
  nrow(mean_score_data) > 0,
  all(complete.cases(mean_score_data))
)
normalized_means <- clean_data %>%
  group_by(dataset, method) %>%
  dplyr::summarise(Mean_Score = mean(scaled_value), .groups = "drop")
df_wide <- left_join(df_wide, normalized_means, by = c("dataset", "method"))


benchmark_axis_spec <- build_metric_axis_spec(
  df_wide,
  c("Mean_Score", metrics)
)


pairwise_upper <- make_pairwise_upper()
pairwise_lower <- make_pairwise_lower(benchmark_axis_spec)
pairwise_diag <- make_pairwise_diag(benchmark_axis_spec)


mean_plots <- map(
  metrics,
  ~ plot_mean_corr(df_wide, .x, benchmark_axis_spec)
)

# Keep each mean-row panel square and separate adjacent axes so the repeated
# numeric tick labels do not collide. A single shared x-axis title replaces the
# five repeated "Mean Score" titles.
mean_row <- wrap_plots(mean_plots, nrow = 1) +
  theme(panel.spacing = grid::unit(1, "lines"))
mean_x_label <- wrap_elements(
  full = grid::textGrob(
    "Mean Score",
    x = grid::unit(0.5, "npc"),
    y = grid::unit(1, "npc"),
    just = c("center", "top"),
    gp = grid::gpar(fontsize = 13)
  ),

)

)

)
mean_panel_label <- wrap_elements(

# ggpairs returns a ggmatrix rather than a ggplot. Its public gtable converter
# lets patchwork compose it with the mean-row plot without changing the matrix.
pairwise_matrix <- ggpairs(
```

# Supp fig 16 A: Plot normalization results

Only reviewed new transformation outputs with the versioned five-metric policy
qualify. Modularity uses k=3; LISI is already higher-is-better separation.
ALR_minCVref selects the minimum-CV reference, and ALR_randref uses its recorded
seeded random reference. Historical summaries with reversed ALR mappings or
missing metrics are rejected rather than relabeled.

```{r}
      method,
      "clr" = "CLR",
```

# Supp fig 16 B: Plot zero imputation results

## Plot results

```{r}
df_zeroimp <- benchmark_zeroimp_scores(benchmark_release, names(datasets))
# Canonical five only: extra stored neighborhood modularities are diagnostics,
# and cannot add panels or replace a missing k=3 score.

df_results_list[["Zero_imputation"]] <- df_zeroimp

df_zeroimp_anosim <- df_zeroimp %>%
  filter(score == "anosim_score") %>%
  group_by(method) %>%
  summarize(mean = mean(value), sem = sd(value) / sqrt(length(value)))
```
