# Supp fig X: ECODA author annotation sensitivity to cell depth

The checked counts-only release retains all five raw separation metrics for
one all-cells baseline and 20 draws at each of nine depths (seeds 101–120).
Compact category counts, exact sample labels and draw/source fingerprints are
saved, so later metric refreshes need no draw replay. This is not summary-only
rescoring of the historical ANOSIM table. Current Bassez uses all 74,948 cells,
26 samples and 40 types; current Stephenson uses the approved 53 samples.

Each panel displays one raw metric, never a mixture of raw metric scales.
Dataset points first average the 20 replicates (the baseline has one row);
bars and standard errors then weight datasets equally. No RNA preprocessing,
model fitting or resampling occurs in this reporting chunk.

```{r fig.width=14, fig.height=9}
if (isTRUE(cell_subsetting_requested) && !is.null(cell_subsetting_results)) {
  cell_subsetting_targets <- c("all cells", "2000", "1000", "500", "400", "300", "200", "150", "100", "50")
  cell_subsetting_dataset_means <- cell_subsetting_results$results %>%
    pivot_longer(all_of(evaluation_metrics()), names_to = "metric", values_to = "value") %>%
    mutate(target = factor(target, levels = cell_subsetting_targets),
      dataset_display = if_else(dataset == "Gongsharma_cmv_young_males", "GongSharma", as.character(dataset)),
      metric = factor(metric, levels = evaluation_metrics())) %>%
    group_by(dataset, dataset_display, target, metric) %>%
    summarise(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop")
  cell_subsetting_aggregate <- cell_subsetting_dataset_means %>%
    group_by(target, metric) %>%
    summarise(se = sd(value) / sqrt(n()), value = mean(value), .groups = "drop")
  p_cell_subsetting <- ggplot() +
    geom_errorbar(data = cell_subsetting_aggregate,
      aes(target, ymin = value - se, ymax = value + se), width = .2) +
    geom_col(data = cell_subsetting_aggregate, aes(target, value), fill = "white", color = "black", width = .9) +
    geom_point(data = cell_subsetting_dataset_means, aes(target, value, shape = dataset_display, color = dataset_display), size = 1.5) +
    geom_line(data = cell_subsetting_dataset_means, aes(target, value, group = dataset_display,
      color = dataset_display, linetype = dataset_display)) +
    scale_shape_manual(values = seq_along(unique(cell_subsetting_dataset_means$dataset_display))) +
    scale_x_discrete(limits = cell_subsetting_targets, drop = FALSE) +
    facet_wrap(~metric, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3, labeller = as_labeller(score_facet_labels)) +
    labs(x = "Cells per sample", y = "Raw separation (higher is better)", color = "Dataset", shape = "Dataset", linetype = "Dataset") +
    theme_classic() + theme(axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1), legend.position = "bottom")
  print(p_cell_subsetting)
  ggsave(file.path(path_plots, "Supp_fig_X_ECODA_authors_HR_cell_subsetting.pdf"),
    plot = p_cell_subsetting, width = 14, height = 9)
}
```

# Exploratory Stephenson UCell activity versus ECODA

The compact exports in the following UCell, CD14, cell-level cutoff and IFN
explorations describe the historical 55-sample cohort. Their exploratory
chunks are disabled for the current 53-sample release after removal of
MH8919226 and MH8919227. Reproduction requires a separate session with the
reviewed historical inputs; old exports must not be mixed with current bundles.

This optional analysis reads only the compact, checksum-verified local export
and cached benchmark results; it never opens the full H5AD, exports data, or
contacts HPC. The raw named list
`stephenson_ucell_matrices` retains all 16 annotation-by-score matrices, including
missing sample/type groups. `stephenson_ucell_coverage` describes every matrix.

The export was generated on Bamboo by `src/extract_stephenson_ucell.py` from the
configured Stephenson benchmark H5AD (418,768 cells; 55 samples), reading only
selected `obs` columns. No minimum-cell cutoff is applied to the exported means;
`stephenson_ucell_artifacts$counts` retains the corresponding sample/type counts
for threshold exploration. The manifest records selected-metadata and output
SHA256 hashes. The original H5AD checksum sidecar is recorded as provenance,
not claimed as a freshly verified whole-file checksum.

Aggregation and feature selection are label independent. For PCA we retain only
cell-type columns that are finite in **every sample** and nonconstant, without
dropping samples. This restriction can be substantial (especially for rare
types); the tables report retained coverage and **names** of excluded columns.
Absent activity is not zero and is never zero-imputed. UCell activities are
centered but **unscaled**, with no CLR or log transform. Matching ECODA features
are aligned by exact sample IDs, not row position; their own complete,
nonconstant feature set need not match the UCell cell-type subset. Labels enter
only after feature selection, for colors and evaluation. ANOSIM, modularity
(k=3), and ARI are recomputed from full feature-space distances, not PC1/2 or
cached benchmark scores. These exploratory scores are not added to the canonical
benchmark results and are not combined into an aggregate score.
Only ANOSIM is displayed on the plots; ARI and modularity remain in the saved tables.

For IFN, arrows can share the same PC1 direction despite correct centering:
the retained cell-type activities are strongly positively correlated.
Centering removes feature means, not shared variation; the axis sign is arbitrary.

All panels use the reference Stephenson benchmark Status colors (Covid:
`#F8766D`; Healthy: `#00BFC4`). PC1–PC2 biplots show feature arrows ranked by
variance-weighted contribution across PC1 and PC2, not additional principal-component
axes: the defaults are up to 12 cell-type loadings for UCell/ECODA and 15 gene loadings
for pseudobulk (adjust the latter to 10–20 below). Fewer arrows are shown when fewer features remain.

The separate gene-expression PCA uses the cached, normalized
`Pseudobulk_hvg2000` matrix, excluding the 155 `IGH`/`IGK`/`IGL`-prefixed features
before PCA (55 samples × 1,845 remaining genes). This is an explicit exploratory
IG exclusion, not the legacy `_bl` bundle: that cached variant is identical to
the unfiltered matrix. Normalization is unchanged; excluded genes are not
replaced by other HVGs. Exact sample IDs and labels are checked before comparison.
No pseudobulk is generated here, and canonical benchmark artifacts remain unchanged.

```{r stephenson_ucell_exploration, eval=FALSE, fig.width=10, fig.height=4}
source("src/notebooks/stephenson_ucell.R")
stephenson_ucell_override <- Sys.getenv("ECODA_STEPHENSON_UCELL_DIR", unset = NA_character_)
stephenson_ucell_root <- if (is.na(stephenson_ucell_override)) {
  file.path("data", "derived", "stephenson_ucell_20261022")
} else {
  stephenson_ucell_override
}

# Adjust these simple variables for interactive exploration.
# Author HR produces UCell + matching ECODA panels side by side.
# HiTME keys (UCell-only) are "hitme_layer1" and "hitme_layer2".
stephenson_ucell_score <- "IFN_UCell"
stephenson_ucell_annotations_selected <- "authors_highres"
stephenson_ucell_n_loadings <- 12L
stephenson_pseudobulk_n_loadings <- 15L
# Other scores: HeatShock_UCell, cellCycle.G1S_UCell, cellCycle.G2M_UCell.

if (is.na(stephenson_ucell_override) && !dir.exists(stephenson_ucell_root)) {
  message("Optional Stephenson UCell section skipped: no compact export at ",
          stephenson_ucell_root)
} else {
  # Explicit override paths must exist; malformed or corrupt artifacts fail.
  stephenson_ucell_artifacts <- load_stephenson_ucell(stephenson_ucell_root)
  stephenson_ucell_matrices <- stephenson_ucell_artifacts$matrices
  stephenson_ucell_coverage <- stephenson_ucell_artifacts$coverage
  print(names(stephenson_ucell_matrices))
  print(stephenson_ucell_coverage, row.names = FALSE)
  stephenson_ucell_comparison <- compare_stephenson_ucell(
    stephenson_ucell_artifacts,
    ecoda_bundles = result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]],
    score = stephenson_ucell_score,
    annotations = stephenson_ucell_annotations_selected,
    n_loadings = stephenson_ucell_n_loadings,
    seed = 20261022L
  )
  print(stephenson_ucell_comparison$table, row.names = FALSE)
  print(stephenson_ucell_comparison$plot)
  if (is.null(result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]][["Pseudobulk_hvg2000"]])) {
    stop("Missing cached Stephenson Pseudobulk_hvg2000 bundle; load the local benchmark results before running this section.")
  }
  stephenson_pseudobulk_comparison <- compare_stephenson_pseudobulk(
    stephenson_ucell_artifacts,
    result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]][["Pseudobulk_hvg2000"]],
    n_loadings = stephenson_pseudobulk_n_loadings,
    seed = 20261022L
  )
  print(stephenson_pseudobulk_comparison$table, row.names = FALSE)
  print(stephenson_pseudobulk_comparison$plot)
  dir.create(path_plots, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  stephenson_ucell_output <- paste0(
    "exploratory_Stephenson_UCell_", stephenson_ucell_score, "_",
    paste(stephenson_ucell_annotations_selected, collapse = "_")
  )
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    file.path(path_plots, paste0(stephenson_ucell_output, ".pdf")),
    plot = stephenson_ucell_comparison$plot, width = 10,
    height = 4 * ceiling(length(stephenson_ucell_comparison$features) / 2)
  )
  utils::write.csv(
    stephenson_ucell_comparison$table,
    file.path(path_plots, paste0(stephenson_ucell_output, "_scores_coverage.csv")),
    row.names = FALSE, na = ""
  )
  utils::write.csv(
    stephenson_ucell_coverage,
    file.path(path_plots, "exploratory_Stephenson_UCell_all_matrix_coverage.csv"),
    row.names = FALSE, na = ""
  )
  stephenson_pseudobulk_output <- "exploratory_Stephenson_Pseudobulk_hvg2000_IGexcluded_PCA"
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    file.path(path_plots, paste0(stephenson_pseudobulk_output, ".pdf")),
    plot = stephenson_pseudobulk_comparison$plot, width = 5, height = 4
  )
  utils::write.csv(
    stephenson_pseudobulk_comparison$table,
    file.path(path_plots, paste0(stephenson_pseudobulk_output, "_scores.csv")),
    row.names = FALSE, na = ""
  )
  utils::write.csv(
    data.frame(gene = stephenson_pseudobulk_comparison$excluded_genes),
    file.path(path_plots, paste0(stephenson_pseudobulk_output, "_excluded_genes.csv")),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}
```

# Exploratory Stephenson author-LR CD14 pseudobulk

This independent optional section reads only a compact local normalized export.
It does not require the UCell export, open an H5AD, access HPC, or insert anything
into `result_list`. The selection is exactly dataset-level
`initial_clustering == "CD14"` (author low resolution), **not** high-resolution
`CD14_mono`. All 55 benchmark samples must be present, each with at least five
selected cells; missing samples are errors, not zero-imputed observations.

Upstream, raw `layers["counts"]` are summed within CD14 by Sample, retaining
all genes for DESeq2 size factors and blind VST. The existing pseudobulk helper
then selects the 2,000 most variable transformed genes **within CD14** using
`hvg=NULL`, `n_hvg=2000`, `black_list="none"`, `batch_col=NULL`, `blind=TRUE`,
and `correct_batch=FALSE`. Only Sample metadata enters that helper. Status is
reserved for evaluation and colors, never normalization, HVG selection, or PCA.
This is plain HVG2000: **no IG exclusion**, unlike the separate whole-sample
pseudobulk exploration above. Actual feature dimensions and minimum/maximum
CD14 cell counts are displayed from the validated export, not inferred from
the whole-sample pseudobulk.

The current export contains 103,326 author-LR CD14 cells across all 55 samples
(159–5,661 cells per sample), summed over 18,561 genes before normalization.
The 55 × 2,000 normalized feature matrix, cell counts, labels, source identity,
and checksums are stored separately from canonical benchmark artifacts.

The centered, unscaled gene-expression PCA uses the same Covid (`#F8766D`) and
Healthy (`#00BFC4`) colors, with 8 contribution-ranked gene arrows by default.
ANOSIM, modularity (k=3), and ARI use full-feature distances. When the local
author-LR/HR ECODA bundles are loaded, their complete sample universes and
Status labels must agree exactly with this export. Scores remain exploratory.
Only ANOSIM is displayed on the plot; the other metrics remain in the saved table.

```{r stephenson_cd14_pseudobulk_exploration, eval=FALSE, fig.width=5, fig.height=4}
source("src/notebooks/stephenson_ucell.R")
stephenson_cd14_override <- Sys.getenv("ECODA_STEPHENSON_CD14_DIR", unset = NA_character_)
stephenson_cd14_root <- if (is.na(stephenson_cd14_override)) {
  file.path("data", "derived", "stephenson_cd14_pseudobulk_20261022")
} else {
  stephenson_cd14_override
}
stephenson_cd14_n_loadings <- 8L

if (is.na(stephenson_cd14_override) && !dir.exists(stephenson_cd14_root)) {
  message("Optional Stephenson CD14 section skipped: no compact export at ",
          stephenson_cd14_root)
} else {
  # An explicitly set override, even empty, must resolve to a valid export.
  stephenson_cd14_bundle <- load_stephenson_cd14_pseudobulk(stephenson_cd14_root)
  if (exists("result_list")) {
    for (method in c("ECODA_authors_LR", "ECODA_authors_HR")) {
      cached <- result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]][[method]]
      if (!is.null(cached)) {
        invisible(align_stephenson_bundle(
          cached, rownames(stephenson_cd14_bundle$feat_mat), stephenson_cd14_bundle$labels
        ))
      }
    }
  }
  validate_stephenson_n_loadings(stephenson_cd14_n_loadings)
  stephenson_cd14_comparison <- stephenson_pca_comparison(
    stephenson_cd14_bundle$feat_mat, stephenson_cd14_bundle$labels,
    title = "CD14+ monocytes pseudobulk: HVG2000",
    n_loadings = stephenson_cd14_n_loadings, seed = 20261022L
  )
  stephenson_cd14_scores <- data.frame(
    method = "Pseudobulk_CD14LR_hvg2000",
    n_samples = nrow(stephenson_cd14_bundle$feat_mat),
    n_features = ncol(stephenson_cd14_bundle$feat_mat),
    min_CD14_cells = min(stephenson_cd14_bundle$metadata$n_cells),
    max_CD14_cells = max(stephenson_cd14_bundle$metadata$n_cells),
    ANOSIM = stephenson_cd14_comparison$ANOSIM,
    modularity_k3 = stephenson_cd14_comparison$modularity_k3,
    ARI = stephenson_cd14_comparison$ARI
  )
  print(stephenson_cd14_scores, row.names = FALSE)
  print(stephenson_cd14_comparison$plot)
  dir.create(path_plots, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  stephenson_cd14_output <- "exploratory_Stephenson_CD14_LR_pseudobulk_hvg2000_PCA"
  ggplot2::ggsave(
    file.path(path_plots, paste0(stephenson_cd14_output, ".pdf")),
    plot = stephenson_cd14_comparison$plot, width = 5, height = 4
  )
  utils::write.csv(
    stephenson_cd14_scores,
    file.path(path_plots, paste0(stephenson_cd14_output, "_scores.csv")),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}
```

# Exploratory Stephenson HiTME composition PCAs

These are two separate PCAs of the cached CLR composition features, not of
sample-distance matrices or UCell means. They retain all benchmark samples,
use centered, unscaled PCA and display ANOSIM from the complete feature space.
Layer 3 includes HiTME functional-state tags; layer 2 does not. No annotations,
positivity cutoffs or canonical benchmark outputs are changed.

```{r stephenson_hitme_pca_exploration, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
source("src/notebooks/stephenson_ucell.R")
if (!exists("result_list") || is.null(result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]])) {
  message("Optional Stephenson HiTME PCAs skipped: no loaded Stephenson bundles.")
} else {
  stephenson_hitme_bundles <- result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]]
  stephenson_hitme_reference <- stephenson_hitme_bundles[["ECODA_authors_HR"]]
  if (is.null(stephenson_hitme_reference)) stop("Missing Stephenson reference labels.")
  stephenson_hitme_ids <- rownames(stephenson_hitme_reference$feat_mat)
  stephenson_hitme_labels <- stephenson_hitme_reference$labels
  stephenson_hitme_methods <- c(
    ECODA_HiTME_HR_layer2 = "HiTME layer 2",
    ECODA_HiTME_HR_layer3 = "HiTME layer 3"
  )
  stephenson_hitme_plots <- stephenson_hitme_score_rows <- list()
  dir.create(path_plots, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (method in names(stephenson_hitme_methods)) {
    bundle <- stephenson_hitme_bundles[[method]]
    if (is.null(bundle)) stop("Missing requested Stephenson bundle: ", method)
    selected <- align_stephenson_bundle(
      bundle, stephenson_hitme_ids, stephenson_hitme_labels
    )
    comparison <- stephenson_pca_comparison(
      selected$features, stephenson_hitme_labels,
      title = paste("Stephenson:", stephenson_hitme_methods[[method]]),
      n_loadings = 8L, seed = 20261026L
    )
    stephenson_hitme_plots[[method]] <- comparison$plot
    stephenson_hitme_score_rows[[method]] <- data.frame(
      method = method, n_samples = nrow(selected$features),
      n_features = ncol(selected$features), ANOSIM = comparison$ANOSIM,
      modularity_k3 = comparison$modularity_k3, ARI = comparison$ARI
    )
    print(comparison$plot)
    prefix <- paste0("exploratory_Stephenson_HiTME_",
                     sub("^ECODA_HiTME_HR_", "", method), "_PCA")
    for (extension in c("pdf", "png")) {
      ggplot2::ggsave(
        file.path(path_plots, paste0(prefix, ".", extension)),
        plot = comparison$plot, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 300
      )
    }
  }
  stephenson_hitme_scores <- do.call(rbind, stephenson_hitme_score_rows)
  rownames(stephenson_hitme_scores) <- NULL
  print(stephenson_hitme_scores, row.names = FALSE)
  utils::write.csv(
    stephenson_hitme_scores,
    file.path(path_plots, "exploratory_Stephenson_HiTME_PCA_scores.csv"),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}
```

# Exploratory Stephenson cell-level UCell cutoff diagnostics

The default HiTME layer-3 rule is **score > 0.2**, strictly, for G1/S, G2/M
and IFN. The new compact metadata export reproduces all 418,768 stored layer-3
annotations with that rule, including HeatShock when checking combined tags.
It contains only selected cell metadata, never expression/count matrices.
Its manifest records source identity, threshold evidence and a verified
SHA256 for the exported Feather file; the full source H5AD was not rehashed.

Each plot pools individual cells across samples and shows every HiTME layer-2
cell type, including an explicit unclassified category. Larger samples have
more weight in these distributions; these are not violins of sample means.
The dashed line is the actual annotation cutoff, not an independently
calibrated biological boundary. In this cohort only 11 cells exceed the IFN
cutoff, so its suitability deserves particular scrutiny. No cutoff is changed.
Median points retain constant or rare categories; missing scores are reported,
not imputed. The CSV reports positive fractions separately for every type.
Each score's axis includes its full observed range and the cutoff; tails are
not removed to enlarge the distributions.

```{r stephenson_ucell_threshold_violins, eval=FALSE, fig.width=22, fig.height=8}
stephenson_cell_score_override <- Sys.getenv(
  "ECODA_STEPHENSON_UCELL_CELLS_DIR", unset = NA_character_
)
stephenson_cell_score_root <- if (is.na(stephenson_cell_score_override)) {
  file.path("data", "derived", "stephenson_ucell_cells_20261026")
} else {
  stephenson_cell_score_override
}
# Change to "full_clustering" for author HR, or "initial_clustering" for author LR.
# Layer 2 avoids grouping cells by the functional tags being evaluated.
stephenson_violin_annotation <- "layer2"
if (is.na(stephenson_cell_score_override) && !dir.exists(stephenson_cell_score_root)) {
  message("Optional cell-level UCell violins skipped: no compact metadata at ",
          stephenson_cell_score_root)
} else {
  stephenson_cell_scores <- load_stephenson_ucell_cell_scores(stephenson_cell_score_root)
  if (exists("result_list") &&
      !is.null(result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]][["ECODA_authors_HR"]])) {
    reference <- result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]][["ECODA_authors_HR"]]
    sample_status <- unique(stephenson_cell_scores$cells[c("Sample", "Status")])
    if (!setequal(sample_status$Sample, names(reference$labels)) ||
        !identical(sample_status$Status[match(names(reference$labels), sample_status$Sample)],
                   as.character(reference$labels))) {
      stop("Cell-score export and Stephenson benchmark samples/labels disagree.")
    }
  }
  stephenson_score_violins <- plot_stephenson_ucell_score_violins(
    stephenson_cell_scores, annotation = stephenson_violin_annotation
  )
  dir.create(path_plots, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
  for (score in names(stephenson_score_violins$plots)) {
    panel <- stephenson_score_violins$plots[[score]]
    print(panel)
    prefix <- paste0("exploratory_Stephenson_UCell_", score, "_violin_",
                     stephenson_violin_annotation)
    for (extension in c("pdf", "png")) {
      ggplot2::ggsave(
        file.path(path_plots, paste0(prefix, ".", extension)),
        plot = panel, width = 22, height = 8, dpi = 200
      )
    }
  }
  utils::write.csv(
    stephenson_score_violins$summary,
    file.path(path_plots, paste0("exploratory_Stephenson_UCell_threshold_summary_",
                                stephenson_violin_annotation, ".csv")),
    row.names = FALSE, na = ""
  )
  print(stephenson_cell_scores$thresholds, row.names = FALSE)
}
```

# Stephenson: Healthy ECODA MDS outliers

The two visually isolated Healthy samples in Supp fig 11 are `MH8919226` and
`MH8919227`. This diagnostic uses the same classical MDS coordinates and
author-HR CLR features as that panel. Raw proportions recover integer counts
by subtracting the stored 0.5 pseudocount. Feature contributions are squared
CLR deviations from the other ten Healthy samples' mean, not causal effects.
The table also includes median proportions among all other 53 samples.
The absence of major T-cell populations explains the distance; its technical
or biological origin is not established by these abundance data.

This is a historical pre-exclusion diagnostic and is disabled for the current
release, which excludes these two samples. Reproducing it requires its original
reviewed historical bundles in a separate analysis session.

```{r stephenson_healthy_outlier_diagnostics, eval=FALSE, fig.width=7, fig.height=5}
if (exists("result_list") &&
    !is.null(result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]][["ECODA_authors_HR"]])) {
  bundle <- result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]][["ECODA_authors_HR"]]
  x <- as.matrix(bundle$feat_mat)
  counts <- as.matrix(bundle$counts) - 0.5
  stopifnot(all(is.finite(counts)), all(counts >= 0), all(counts == floor(counts)),
            identical(dimnames(counts), dimnames(x)))
  outliers <- c("MH8919226", "MH8919227")
  stopifnot(all(outliers %in% rownames(x)),
            all(bundle$labels[outliers] == "Healthy"))
  healthy_reference <- bundle$labels == "Healthy" & !rownames(x) %in% outliers
  proportions <- 100 * counts / rowSums(counts)
  driver_rows <- lapply(outliers, function(id) {
    delta <- x[id, ] - colMeans(x[healthy_reference, , drop = FALSE])
    data.frame(
      Sample = id, cell_type = colnames(x), n_cells = counts[id, ],
      percent = proportions[id, ],
      other_healthy_median_percent = apply(
        proportions[healthy_reference, , drop = FALSE], 2, stats::median
      ),
      other_samples_median_percent = apply(
        proportions[!rownames(x) %in% outliers, , drop = FALSE], 2, stats::median
      ),
      delta_CLR = delta,
      distance_contribution_percent = 100 * delta^2 / sum(delta^2),
      row.names = NULL
    )
  })
  stephenson_outlier_drivers <- do.call(rbind, driver_rows)
  stephenson_outlier_drivers <- stephenson_outlier_drivers[
    order(stephenson_outlier_drivers$Sample,
          -stephenson_outlier_drivers$distance_contribution_percent), ]
  mds <- stats::cmdscale(bundle$dist_mat, k = 2)
  highlight <- data.frame(
    Sample = outliers, Dim1 = mds[outliers, 1], Dim2 = mds[outliers, 2]
  )
  stephenson_outlier_plot <- plot_mds(
    bundle$dist_mat, bundle$labels, cluster_score = FALSE, mod_score = FALSE,
    anosim_score = FALSE, title = "Stephenson ECODA: Healthy outliers"
  ) + ggrepel::geom_text_repel(
    data = highlight, ggplot2::aes(x = Dim1, y = Dim2, label = Sample),
    inherit.aes = FALSE, seed = 20261026L, size = 3
  )
  print(stephenson_outlier_plot)
  for (extension in c("pdf", "png")) {
    ggplot2::ggsave(
      file.path(path_plots, paste0("exploratory_Stephenson_Healthy_outliers_MDS.", extension)),
      plot = stephenson_outlier_plot, width = 7, height = 5, dpi = 200
    )
  }
  utils::write.csv(
    stephenson_outlier_drivers,
    file.path(path_plots, "exploratory_Stephenson_Healthy_outlier_abundance_drivers.csv"),
    row.names = FALSE
  )
}
```

# Exploratory Stephenson author-annotation abundances

Each box pools all 55 samples for one author-defined cell type; points show
individual samples, with Covid in red and Healthy in cyan. Crosses identify
the Healthy outliers `MH8919226` and `MH8919227` (not additional observations).
Percentages use recovered raw integer counts and preserve true zeros. CLR
values are the cached features: `log(raw count + 0.5)` minus its within-sample
mean across all cell types, not a transform of percentages.

This historical 55-sample diagnostic is disabled for the current release.

```{r stephenson_author_abundance_boxplots, eval=FALSE, fig.width=c(12,12,20,20), fig.height=c(6,6,7,7)}
if (!exists("result_list") || is.null(result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]])) {
  message("Optional Stephenson author abundance plots skipped: no loaded Stephenson bundles.")
} else {
  stephenson_author_abundance <- local({
    bundles <- result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]]
    methods <- c(ECODA_authors_LR = "authors_LR", ECODA_authors_HR = "authors_HR")
    outliers <- c("MH8919226", "MH8919227")
    tables <- plots <- list()
    reference_labels <- NULL
    dir.create(path_plots, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    for (method in names(methods)) {
      bundle <- bundles[[method]]
      if (is.null(bundle)) stop("Missing requested Stephenson bundle: ", method)
      counts <- as.matrix(bundle$counts)
      clr <- as.matrix(bundle$feat_mat)
      ids <- rownames(counts)
      types <- colnames(counts)
      labels <- bundle$labels
      stopifnot(
        is.numeric(counts), is.numeric(clr),
        nrow(counts) == 55L, ncol(counts) > 0L,
        !is.null(ids), !anyNA(ids), all(nzchar(ids)), !anyDuplicated(ids),
        !is.null(types), !anyNA(types), all(nzchar(types)), !anyDuplicated(types),
        identical(dimnames(counts), dimnames(clr)),
        identical(names(labels), ids), !anyNA(labels),
        all(as.character(labels) %in% c("Covid", "Healthy")),
        sum(labels == "Covid") == 43L, sum(labels == "Healthy") == 12L,
        all(is.finite(counts)), all(is.finite(clr))
      )
      raw <- counts - 0.5
      stopifnot(
        all(raw >= 0), all(raw == floor(raw)), all(rowSums(raw) > 0),
        isTRUE(all.equal(clr, log(counts) - rowMeans(log(counts)),
                         tolerance = 1e-10, check.attributes = FALSE)),
        all(outliers %in% ids), all(labels[outliers] == "Healthy")
      )
      if (!is.null(reference_labels)) {
        stopifnot(setequal(ids, names(reference_labels)),
                  identical(as.character(labels),
                            as.character(reference_labels[ids])))
      }
      reference_labels <- labels
      percent <- 100 * raw / rowSums(raw)
      annotation <- unname(methods[[method]])
      tab <- data.frame(
        Sample = rep(ids, times = length(types)),
        Status = rep(as.character(labels), times = length(types)),
        celltype = rep(types, each = length(ids)),
        annotation = annotation, percent = as.vector(percent),
        CLR = as.vector(clr), stringsAsFactors = FALSE
      )
      tab$is_outlier <- tab$Sample %in% outliers
      tables[[annotation]] <- tab
      tab$celltype <- factor(tab$celltype, levels = types)
      tab$Status <- factor(tab$Status, levels = c("Covid", "Healthy"))
      tab$sample_marker <- factor(
        ifelse(tab$is_outlier, "Healthy outliers", "Other samples"),
        levels = c("Other samples", "Healthy outliers")
      )
      for (measure in c("percent", "CLR")) {
        tab$value <- tab[[measure]]
        panel <- ggplot2::ggplot(tab, ggplot2::aes(x = celltype, y = value)) +
          ggplot2::geom_boxplot(
            fill = "white", colour = "black", outlier.shape = NA, width = 0.65
          ) +
          ggplot2::geom_point(
            ggplot2::aes(colour = Status, shape = sample_marker),
            position = ggplot2::position_jitter(
              width = 0.18, height = 0, seed = 20261027L
            ), size = 1.6, alpha = 0.8
          ) +
          ggplot2::scale_colour_manual(
            values = c(Covid = "#F8766D", Healthy = "#00BFC4"), drop = FALSE
          ) +
          ggplot2::scale_shape_manual(
            values = c("Other samples" = 16, "Healthy outliers" = 4), drop = FALSE
          ) +
          ggplot2::labs(
            title = paste("Stephenson:", gsub("_", " ", annotation), measure),
            x = "Cell type", y = if (measure == "percent") "Raw cell percentage (%)" else "CLR",
            colour = "Status", shape = "Sample",
            caption = paste(
              "Crosses: Healthy MH8919226 and MH8919227. Raw percentages preserve zeros;",
              "CLR = log(raw count + 0.5) minus the within-sample mean log count."
            )
          ) +
          ggplot2::theme_classic() +
          ggplot2::theme(
            axis.text.x = ggplot2::element_text(angle = 60, hjust = 1, colour = "black"),
            axis.text.y = ggplot2::element_text(colour = "black"),
            legend.position = "top"
          )
        plots[[paste(annotation, measure, sep = "_")]] <- panel
        print(panel)
        prefix <- paste0("exploratory_Stephenson_", annotation, "_", measure, "_boxplot")
        for (extension in c("pdf", "png")) {
          ggplot2::ggsave(
            file.path(path_plots, paste0(prefix, ".", extension)),
            plot = panel, width = if (annotation == "authors_HR") 20 else 12,
            height = if (annotation == "authors_HR") 7 else 6, dpi = 300
          )
        }
      }
    }
    tidy <- do.call(rbind, tables)
    rownames(tidy) <- NULL
    utils::write.csv(
      tidy, file.path(path_plots, "exploratory_Stephenson_author_abundances.csv"),
      row.names = FALSE
    )
    list(table = tidy, plots = plots)
  })
}
```

# Exploratory Stephenson author-HR IFN-responding composition PCA

This is count splitting, not duplicate augmentation: each cell with
`IFN_UCell > 0.1` moves from its author-HR type into that type's
`*_IFN_responding` state. Equality at 0.1 is nonresponding. Original names
contain only the remaining cells; unobserved responding states are omitted.
Every cell and sample is retained, and disease labels are used only for
evaluation/plotting, never to assign states. This exploratory threshold does
not change the HiTME annotation rule of strictly greater than 0.2 or its
manifest. PCA uses centered, unscaled CLR of split raw counts plus 0.5;
ANOSIM uses the complete CLR feature space, not only the displayed PCs.

```{r stephenson_author_hr_ifn_pca, eval=FALSE, fig.width=8, fig.height=6}
source("src/notebooks/stephenson_ucell.R")
if (!exists("result_list") || is.null(result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]])) {
  message("Optional Stephenson author-HR IFN PCA skipped: no loaded Stephenson bundles.")
} else {
  stephenson_author_hr_ifn <- local({
    bundle <- result_list[["bmark"]][["Stephenson"]][["ECODA_authors_HR"]]
    if (is.null(bundle)) stop("Missing requested Stephenson bundle: ECODA_authors_HR")
    override <- Sys.getenv("ECODA_STEPHENSON_UCELL_CELLS_DIR", unset = NA_character_)
    root <- if (is.na(override)) {
      file.path("data", "derived", "stephenson_ucell_cells_20261026")
    } else {
      override
    }
    if (is.na(override) && !dir.exists(root)) {
      message("Optional Stephenson author-HR IFN PCA skipped: no compact metadata at ", root)
      return(NULL)
    }
    artifacts <- load_stephenson_ucell_cell_scores(root)
    split <- stephenson_ifn_split_composition(artifacts, bundle, threshold = 0.1)
    comparison <- stephenson_pca_comparison(
      split$feat_mat, split$labels,
      title = "Stephenson: author HR split by IFN_UCell > 0.1",
      n_loadings = 8L, seed = 20261027L
    )
    prefix <- "exploratory_Stephenson_authors_HR_IFNresponding_threshold0.1_PCA"
    dir.create(path_plots, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
    print(comparison$plot)
    for (extension in c("pdf", "png")) {
      ggplot2::ggsave(
        file.path(path_plots, paste0(prefix, ".", extension)),
        plot = comparison$plot, width = 8, height = 6, dpi = 300
      )
    }
    scores <- data.frame(
      method = "authors_HR_IFNresponding", threshold = split$threshold,
      n_samples = nrow(split$feat_mat), n_features = ncol(split$feat_mat),
      ANOSIM = comparison$ANOSIM, modularity_k3 = comparison$modularity_k3,
      ARI = comparison$ARI
    )
    # Match the split analysis on the complete original CLR feature space.
    original_distances <- stats::dist(bundle$feat_mat)
    set.seed(20261027L)
    original_anosim <- unname(
      vegan::anosim(original_distances, split$labels, parallel = 1)$statistic
    )
    set.seed(20261027L)
    original_ari <- clust_eval(original_distances, split$labels)
    set.seed(20261027L)
    original_modularity <- calc_modularity(original_distances, split$labels, knn_k = 3)
    scores <- rbind(
      data.frame(
        method = "authors_HR_original", threshold = NA_real_,
        n_samples = nrow(bundle$feat_mat), n_features = ncol(bundle$feat_mat),
        ANOSIM = original_anosim, modularity_k3 = original_modularity,
        ARI = original_ari
      ),
      scores
    )
    print(scores, row.names = FALSE)
    utils::write.csv(
      scores, file.path(path_plots, paste0(prefix, "_scores.csv")), row.names = FALSE
    )
    utils::write.csv(
      data.frame(Sample = rownames(split$raw_counts), split$raw_counts,
                 check.names = FALSE),
      file.path(path_plots, paste0(prefix, "_raw_counts.csv")), row.names = FALSE
    )
    utils::write.csv(
      split$per_type, file.path(path_plots, paste0(prefix, "_per_type.csv")),
      row.names = FALSE
    )
    utils::write.csv(
      split$feature_map, file.path(path_plots, paste0(prefix, "_feature_map.csv")),
      row.names = FALSE
    )
    list(composition = split, comparison = comparison, scores = scores)
  })
}
```

## MDS for all datasets

The methods, dataset scope, distances, and group labels match Supp figs 3–13.
Separation Score is the arithmetic mean of all five metrics after min–max
normalization across Figure 2A's full default pool, including the saved NULL
baseline, within each dataset/evaluation, even when NULL is not drawn.
The stored per-metric values remain raw and are labeled separately.

```{r presentation_mds, fig.height=7, fig.width=18}
presentation_mds_methods <- methods_in_scope_named(list(
  "ECODA_authors_HR" = "ECODA",
  "Pseudobulk_hvg2000" = "Pseudobulk",
  "GloScope_hvg2000_pcadims30" = "GloScope",
  "GloProp" = "GloProp",
  "MrVI_hvg2000" = "MrVI",
  "scPoli_hvg2000_dims15_highres" = "scPoli",
  "MOFA_hvg2000_factors15" = "MOFA",
  "PILOT_hvg2000" = "PILOT",
  "scITD_hvg2000_factors5" = "scITD",
  "QOT_hvg2000" = "QOT",
  "PILOT-GM-VAE_hvg2000" = "PILOT-GM-VAE"
))
presentation_score_names <- benchmark_metrics

for (ds in names(result_list[["bmark"]])) {
  presentation_mds_plots <- list()
  presentation_label_levels <- sort(unique(unlist(lapply(
    names(presentation_mds_methods), function(m) {
      as.character(result_list[["bmark"]][[ds]][[m]][["labels"]])
    }
  ))))
  if (ds == "Bassez") {
    presentation_label_levels <- c("Expander", "Non-expander")
  }

  for (m in names(presentation_mds_methods)) {
    bundle <- result_list[["bmark"]][[ds]][[m]]
    labels <- as.character(bundle$labels)
    if (ds == "Bassez") {
      labels <- as.character(benchmark_pca_display_labels(labels, "Bassez"))
    }
    labels <- factor(labels, levels = presentation_label_levels)
    presentation_scores <- vapply(
      presentation_score_names, function(s) bundle$scores[[s]], numeric(1)
    )
    stopifnot(all(is.finite(presentation_scores)))

    presentation_mds_plots[[m]] <- plot_mds(
      bundle$dist_mat, labels,
      cluster_score = FALSE, mod_score = FALSE, anosim_score = FALSE,
      coord_equal = TRUE, pointsize = 2,
      title = presentation_mds_methods[[m]]
    ) +
      labs(subtitle = sprintf(
        "Five-metric min–max mean: %.2f",
        benchmark_normalized_mean(df_benchmark, ds, m, benchmark_main_normalization_methods)
      )) +
      scale_color_discrete(limits = presentation_label_levels, drop = FALSE) +
      guides(shape = "none")
    if (ds == "Bassez") presentation_mds_plots[[m]] <- presentation_mds_plots[[m]] + labs(color = "Clonal expansion")
  }

  presentation_mds_plot <- wrap_plots(presentation_mds_plots) +
    plot_layout(nrow = 2, guides = "collect") &
    theme(legend.position = "bottom")
  print(presentation_mds_plot)
  ggsave(
    file.path(path_plots, paste0("presentation_mds_", ds, ".pdf")),
    plot = presentation_mds_plot, width = 18, height = 7
  )
}
```

## Zhang: frequency versus ECODA PCA

The two PCA plots use author high-resolution cell types without cell-type
arrows or labels. Scores use the complete feature-space distances, not just
PC1–PC2.
The shared tissue legend sits between the panels.

```{r presentation_pca_zhang, fig.height=3.85, fig.width=8.4}
presentation_pca_methods <- c(
  "Freq_highres" = "Cell type frequency (%)",
  "ECODA_authors_HR" = "ECODA"
)
if ("Zhang" %in% names(result_list[["bmark"]])) {
  presentation_pca_plots <- lapply(names(presentation_pca_methods), function(m) {
    bundle <- result_list[["bmark"]][["Zhang"]][[m]]
    labels <- factor(bundle$labels)
    levels(labels) <- tools::toTitleCase(levels(labels))

    plot_pca(
      feat_mat = bundle$feat_mat, labels = labels,
      title = presentation_pca_methods[[m]],
      cluster_score = TRUE, mod_score = TRUE, anosim_score = TRUE,
      knn_k = 3, pointsize = 3, coord_equal = TRUE,
      invisible = c("var", "quali")
    ) +
      labs(color = "Tissue", shape = "Tissue")
  })

  presentation_pca_zhang <- wrap_plots(
    presentation_pca_plots[[1]], guide_area(), presentation_pca_plots[[2]],
    nrow = 1, widths = c(1, 0.3, 1), guides = "collect"
  ) & theme(legend.position = "right")
  print(presentation_pca_zhang)
  ggsave(
    file.path(path_plots, "presentation_pca_Zhang.pdf"),
    plot = presentation_pca_zhang, width = 8.4, height = 3.85
  )
}
```
